one_sentence: Five independent theorems prove the universe is not a closed system, requiring an external, self-grounding source of coherence identified as the Logos.
executive_summary: This document argues that five established theorems from logic, linguistics, computation, thermodynamics, and information theory independently prove that closed systems cannot sustain themselves. Since the universe has maintained order, truth, and coherence for 13.8 billion years, it cannot be a closed system. The document further claims that good and evil are measurable as coherence and decoherence, respectively, and that these measurements are universal across domains. The necessary external source of coherence must be necessary, self-grounding, and the origin of all order—properties that align with the theological concept of the Logos. The conclusion is that multiple independent paths of inquiry converge on the same reality.
short_summary: This document is a philosophical and scientific argument for the existence of a transcendent ground of reality. It claims that five theorems from different fields prove closed systems collapse, yet the universe persists, implying it is not closed. Key evidence includes the universality of coherence/decoherence as measurable across physics, biology, ethics, and theology. This matters because it suggests that science and theology converge on a single necessary foundation.
